item.title: Gen Z: Quiet Quitting Comes to India. AI Will Make It Worse
item.description: Doomsday predictions of artificial intelligence causing massive white-collar job losses haven’t come to pass. At least not yet. There is, however, evidence that AI tools, while helping experts become more productive, are hollowing out the skills that young people acquire early in their careers. This divergence may be showing up as a big jump in “quiet quitting” — a lack of meaningful workplace connection — even in an economy like India’s, where youth are starved of decent employment.
item.dc:creator: Andy Mukherjee

item.title: Your $30 Jeans Are Running Out of Cheap Power in Bangladesh
item.description: For decades, the fast fashion filling your closet has depended on a simple equation.
item.dc:creator: David Fickling

item.title: Trump Is Setting Up the UN and Its Next Leader for Failure
item.description: How risible and despicable: In addressing the United Nations General Assembly, Donald Trump once again bragged that “while others have spoken of peace, I have made peace.” Then he rattled off the “eight” wars he has supposedly settled, before boasting about the war he waged and won against Venezuela and defending the war he is waging, but seems unable to win, against Iran, even musing about whether to “annihilate” it.
item.dc:creator: Andreas Kluth

item.title: Youth Sports’ Stay-to-Play Is Coercion by Another Name
item.description: The bill for a season in youth sports comes in installments: new skates, registration fees and uniforms. Then there’s the price of travel tournaments, gas and restaurant meals. Finally, the hotel requirement, which feels like one mandate too many. Families are instructed to stay at a designated hotel, or their children — and even their team — may not play.
item.dc:creator: Adam Minter

item.title: AI Is Devastating Local News. Who Will Hold City Hall Accountable?
item.description: If AI hasn’t finished off your local newspaper yet, just wait. It will. OpenAI, the company that built ChatGPT, has called itself an “existential threat” to news publishers.
item.dc:creator: Mary Ellen Klas

item.title: Panama’s Giant Copper Mine Is Too Valuable to Waste
item.description: Copper prices are hitting records as the world struggles with shortages. Why on earth is a giant $10 billion mine that accounts for about 1.5% of global production sitting idle in the Panamanian jungle?
item.dc:creator: Juan Pablo Spinetto

item.title: Warren Buffet Son Howard Buffett Is the Right Kind of Nepo Baby
item.description: Facts are facts, so let’s just state it plainly: Howard Buffett is a nepo baby. And this is one of the rare cases where I think we should be OK with it.
item.dc:creator: Beth Kowitt

item.title: With Westinghouse, US's Nuclear Champion Follows an Old Playbook
item.description: For all the buzz of small modular reactors and artificial intelligence hyperscalers, the rebirth of the US nuclear power industry looks increasingly old-school. Westinghouse Electric Co. is reportedly set to soon file publicly for a $50 billion initial public offering, and it is no startup. Westinghouse supplied the reactor for America’s first large-scale civilian nuclear power station and traces back to 1886.
item.dc:creator: Liam Denning

item.title: This Historic Divide Between Bulls and Bears Signals a Slowdown
item.description: There’s a fierce disagreement between bulls and bears about the health of the US stock market, and the two sides could not be further apart. Bulls see more big gains from historic corporate prosperity fueled by new technology; bears see a dangerous bubble built on hype around artificial intelligence. Both are wrong.
item.dc:creator: Nir Kaissar

item.title: Nvidia's Huang Is a Gatekeeper on AI Regulation
item.description: Pick your favorite doomsday scenario for artificial intelligence. Whatever you choose, the road to prevention likely runs through Jensen Huang.
item.dc:creator: Parmy Olson

item.title: Why the Russia Election Actually Matters to Ukraine and Europe
item.description: In what must be the world’s least surprising election result, parties loyal to President Vladimir Putin have made a clean sweep in elections to Russia’s parliament, the State Duma. There’s little purpose to parsing who won what share of the vote; the point is that opponents of Putin and his war were either jailed, dead, in exile or banned from running. As a democratic exercise, this signified nothing — but it was an important moment nonetheless.
item.dc:creator: Marc Champion

item.title: France Is Living in Denial
item.description: A lengthy, two-part biopic of a mid-century politician would be an unlikely hit in most countries. But not, apparently, if the politician is Charles de Gaulle and the country is France. The films based on Julian Jackson’s 2018 biography of the general have seized the country’s imagination. They opened to a mere 380,000 viewers in their first days of screening, though — like de Gaulle himself — they grew in the telling. More than 5.5 million French people have seen them now.
item.dc:creator: Mihir Sharma

item.title: Erdogan: The UN Must End the Security Council Veto
item.description: The tragedies of recent years, including pandemics, energy crises, disruptions to supply chains and regional conflicts, have demonstrated that leaving the resolution of global crises to the will of a handful of capitals is no longer compatible with the realities of today’s world. The adaptation of global decision-making mechanisms to today’s circumstances can no longer be postponed.
item.dc:creator: Recep Tayyip Erdogan

item.title: Oil Market: Iran War Supertankers Charge $1 Million a Day
item.description: Who’s winning the Iran war? The supertanker tycoons charging an arm and leg to cross Hormuz.
item.dc:creator: Jessica Karl

item.title: Jollibee Shouldn’t Rush Its Global IPO
item.description: Jollibee Foods Corp. has spent two decades building a global restaurant empire. But while it makes sense for the Philippines’ fast-food powerhouse to separate the burgeoning international business from its mature, domestic operations, it shouldn’t rush to take the new company public.
item.dc:creator: Juliana Liu
